retrieval_cards.prompt: Give the route for the human element and fatigue question.
retrieval_cards.answer: 1 What the human element means in STCW. 2 Competence-based standards. 3 Fitness for duty. 4 Responsibility on companies and Administrations. 5 The IMO guidance on fatigue - MSC.1/Circ.1598 and its six modules. 6 How the guidance and the mandatory rules fit together.
retrieval_cards.why: Steps 1 to 4 are limb A's 8 marks, steps 5 and 6 limb B's. Keeping competence in A and the Guidelines in B stops the two limbs duplicating each other.

retrieval_cards.prompt: State the minimum hours of rest under the Manila-amended section A-VIII/1.
retrieval_cards.answer: Not less than 10 hours in any 24-hour period and 77 hours in any 7-day period. The daily rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which shall be at least 6 hours, and the interval between consecutive periods of rest shall not exceed 14 hours.
retrieval_cards.why: The 14-hour interval is the provision most often omitted, and its absence from a source is the quickest way to tell that the source is pre-Manila.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Is the weekly minimum rest 70 hours or 77 hours?
retrieval_cards.answer: 77 hours in any 7-day period is the norm. 70 hours is the floor that applies only where an exception has been authorised, and such an exception may not run for more than two consecutive weeks. Both figures are real; they do different jobs.
retrieval_cards.why: A widely available official IMO circular copy of A-VIII/1 is the pre-Manila 1995 text and gives 70 as the weekly figure. It is official and superseded - always check the edition.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Which circular is the IMO guidance on fatigue, and what did it replace?
retrieval_cards.answer: MSC.1/Circ.1598, Guidelines on fatigue, dated 24 January 2019 and approved at the 100th session of the Maritime Safety Committee. It supersedes MSC/Circ.1014 on Guidance on fatigue mitigation and management, approved at MSC 74 in 2001. It is recommendatory, not mandatory.
retrieval_cards.why: Limb B says 'the IMO guidance' - a specific document. Naming it and its predecessor is most of the eight marks.

retrieval_cards.prompt: List the six modules of MSC.1/Circ.1598.
retrieval_cards.answer: 1 Fatigue - what it is and its causes. 2 Fatigue and the Company. 3 Fatigue and the Seafarer. 4 Fatigue Awareness and Training. 5 Fatigue and Ship Design. 6 Fatigue, the Administration and Port State Authorities.
retrieval_cards.why: Each module is addressed to a different party, which is the structural point: fatigue is managed by the company, the individual, the designer and the regulator, not only by the watchkeeper.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What did the Manila amendments add to STCW on the human element?
retrieval_cards.answer: Mandatory training in leadership and teamworking at operational level and in leadership and managerial skill at management level - bringing engine-room and bridge resource management, situational awareness and workload management into the Convention; revised and tightened rest-hour requirements in section A-VIII/1 including the 14-hour interval rule; and alcohol limits for masters, officers and seafarers with designated safety, security and environmental duties.
retrieval_cards.why: The teamworking addition is the recognition that technically competent individuals still fail as a crew, which is the analytical heart of limb A.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Your engineer's rest-hour record is exactly compliant every single week. Is that reassuring?
retrieval_cards.answer: No - it is a warning. The Guidelines are explicit that hours of rest are a prescriptive formula and that complying with the formula is not the same as being rested; circadian rhythm and sleep debt determine whether rest is restorative. A record that is always exactly at the limit suggests the limit is driving the record rather than the work.
retrieval_cards.why: This is the management-level judgement the question is really testing, and it is what separates a Class I answer from a recitation of numbers.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What does STCW regulation I/14 require of the company?
retrieval_cards.answer: That seafarers assigned to its ships hold valid certificates, are familiarised with their specific duties and with the ship's arrangements, installations, equipment and procedures before being assigned duties, and that documentation and data are maintained. It places the human element on the company rather than leaving it as an individual's problem.
retrieval_cards.why: Limb A is incomplete without the responsibility front, and I/14 is the provision that supplies it.
